newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico net assets rise, reserves fall.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico net assets rise, reserves fall.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said on Tuesday its net international assets as of March 14 were $10.783 billion, compared to $10.519 billion on March 7.
The central bank said that its net international reserves as of March 14 were $20.176 billion, compared to $20.339 billion as of March 7.
The central bank said the increase of $264 million in net international assets in the same time period was due to:

--Net purchases of $160 million in foreign debt from the federal government. It added that the Banco de Mexico last Friday pre-paid $200 million in liabilities to the IMF, a payment which did not affect the level of net assets.
--Net income from operations by the state oil company Pemex worth $114 million.

--A net loss of $10 million dollars for a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts from commercial banks at the central bank.
Banco de Mexico said that between March 7 and March 14 the monetary base rose by 2.854 billion pesos due to an increase in seasonal demand for bills and coins.

During that week, federal government deposits in the central bank fell 9.261 billion pesos, the difference between government spending and income from tax revenues. It said payments to teachers were a major item in public spending.

To compensate for the increased liquidity resulting from the various operations of the federal government, Banco de Mexico said it had received 8.335 billion pesos in deposits that banks had constituted with the central bank.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's reserves and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
Mar 7 Mar 14
International Reserves
U.S. Dollars $20.339 bln $20.176 bln
Monetary Base 74.104 76.958
Net International Assets*
U.S. Dollars $10.519 bln $10.783 bln
Net Domestic Credit -10.206 -9.078
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six-month duration from other central banks.
((--David Luhnow, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7902))
